kernel_of_truth.description: The dome defender's 'perspective cuts both ways' move correctly identifies that crepuscular divergence at the sun and anticrepuscular convergence at the anti-solar point are not two independent optical phenomena but a single perspective effect viewed from two parts of the celestial sphere (data/wins.json:WIN-026 detail_evidence ~'Perspective collapses lines to a vanishing point only where the underlying rays are mutually parallel'). That is a real geometric fact about projective geometry. The dome author has spotted a genuine symmetry, and the EXP-282 paragraph integrated at c5 acknowledges it explicitly before turning it against the local-sun claim.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The symmetry is precisely what makes two-horizon convergence a DISCRIMINATOR rather than ambiguous evidence (data/wins.json:WIN-026 detail_evidence ~'Two-horizon convergence is therefore a discriminator'). Both vanishing points exist together if and only if the underlying rays are mutually parallel — this is the projective-geometry definition of a vanishing point. A finite source emits non-parallel rays whose sky projections share the source point but never its antipode; the symmetric perspective the defender invokes does not apply because the rays are not parallel. The kernel ('perspective explains both ends') is the very fact that rules out a finite-altitude source. The PATCH-380-A integration this cycle adds verifiable provenance (monitor.py:~852 hardcodes 5,733 on both sides — confirmed by raw-text/07-ai-context.txt:24's own admission that '5,733 km Sun altitude is an OPTICAL illusion'), so the structural argument is now anchored in both the dome's published parameters and its own AI-context documentation.

advocate_mode.best_defense: The dome defender now confronts an empirical citation in our review ('predicted: "5733", observed: "5733", monitor.py line ~852'). The strongest fair-minded counter-move is to concede the hardcoding is real but reframe its purpose: 'monitor.py is a documentation/dashboard layer for an already-validated model parameter, not the validation layer. The empirical validation for the 5,733 km figure lives in the crepuscular-ray geometry itself, which monitor.py is not designed to (and cannot) reproduce — image-based geometry verification is not a monitor.py-class task. Our model documentation explicitly labels 5,733 km an optical illusion of aetheric refraction; this concession at the model layer means monitor.py honestly reports a parametric figure and is not the validation target our critics imply.' This is a re-categorisation move: 'monitoring is dashboard, not validation' — it accepts the structural fact but tries to defuse the rhetorical sting.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Already partially preempted by our review's framing ('There is no operational sense in which this is a prospective prediction of a real measurement'). The reframe-as-dashboard move is weak because the dome model itself publishes WIN-026 in a list called 'predictions' and 'wins' — the 67 confirmed predictions framing is how the model recruits its credibility. If WIN-026 is dashboard-not-validation, then by symmetry the rest of the WIN catalogue's confirmation count is overstated. Optional one-sentence preemption: 'The dome model's site lists WIN-026 in a 67-prediction confirmation tally — the WIN claims confirmation, not dashboard reporting; a defender who reframes monitor.py as dashboard implicitly concedes WIN-026's place in the confirmation count is overstated.' Not blocking — defense_survives=2 is well within the floor where verbal preemption is rhetorical polish rather than defender-bait.
